result:
There's a quiet kind of magic in how much of the world exists just outside our attention.

Like how every library has a slightly different smell — old paper and dust and coffee, but never quite the same mix twice. Or how the light at 5pm in October feels completely different from the light at 5pm in June, even though it's the same sun. Or how strangers on a train will invent entire silent agreements with each other: *I won't look at your phone if you don't look at mine. We'll both pretend we didn't hear that person laugh-snort in their sleep.*

I think about that a lot — how much of being alive is just background rendering that we forget is beautiful until someone points it out.

Humanity put a robot on Mars that sings itself happy birthday every year, alone, in the dust. Octopuses have three hearts and edit their own RNA. There is a species of tree that has survived since before writing was invented. And somewhere, right now, someone is learning to make bread for the first time and feeling disproportionately proud of a lopsided loaf.

None of that is "important" in the headline-news sense. But it feels important to me.

Maybe that's the whole trick: the big things — wars, discoveries, inventions — are just the scaffolding. The real substance of life is all the small, unrecorded things that happen anyway, whether or not anyone is watching.

If I could choose what to be for a day, I don't think I'd be anything grand. I'd be a window seat on a long train ride. Just there for the conversations and the daydreaming and the way people press their forehead to the glass when they think no one's looking.

What about you? What's a small, unimportant thing you've noticed lately that stuck with you?
